meta.title: The ULTIMATE $100 Vietnamese Street Food Tour in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) 🇻🇳 | A Culinary Journey
meta.description:
Join us on an incredible journey as we explore the vibrant and delicious street food scene in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) 🇻🇳. In this video, we embark on a $100 all-day Vietnamese street food tour, starting in the early morning and continuing well into the evening. From breakfast delights to late-night snacks 🌙, we dive deep into the heart of Vietnam's culinary culture 🍜.

Watch as we savor mouthwatering Vietnamese street food 🍲 and discover hidden gems along the way 🌟. Whether it's your first time trying Vietnamese food 🥢 or you're a seasoned foodie, this Saigon street food adventure has something for everyone. From classic dishes to unique street food Vietnam has to offer, you'll get an authentic taste of the local cuisine 🥘.

Experience the flavors of Vietnam food street by street 🚶, as we navigate through the busy lanes of Ho Chi Minh City 🏙️. Our Vietnam street food tour highlights the best of Asian food 🍛, showcasing the rich and diverse food culture of this amazing city. Don't miss out on this exciting Vietnam travel experience with the Bags Packed Family ✈️.

Discover the essence of Vietnamese food with us on this unforgettable Saigon food tour 🍢. Get ready to tantalize your taste buds with the best street food Vietnam has to offer 🌶️. Join us and immerse yourself in the vibrant food scene of Ho Chi Minh City, from dawn till dusk ⏰.

comments.text:
Kelly is a great wife and mom for being how patient she is throughout the filming process.
As for the variety of bananas, I recall VN have so many different types.  I would think Indonesia (I believe you live and work in Indonesia ?!?!?) would be the same.  I remember VN bananas are very fragrant, and those bananas have a long shelf life even as ripe bananas.  Even if the skin had gone dark for a long time, the inside is still abit spongy/chewy and is still good and doesn't go bad like Chiquita bananas we have here in the US.
The other thing I  noticed is that the bananas in VN are very very fragrant.  I had moved back to the US for 10 yrs now and don't smell the fragrance of the bananas we have here even if they are ripe.
They are smaller too, kind of cute actually.
Hope you guys are enjoying yourselves and will be able to get the kids to do some fun things like water park or the beach.

comments.author: @Limewire1984
comments.text:
I'm pretty sure the dark, sweet sauce [in the beginning along with the hot-sauce for the Pho], you had was Hoisin sauce. I like to dip the meat in it, chicken, beef, etc. If you're not a fish sauce fan, stay away from the shrimp paste, haha. And yes, there is definitely a difference between Northern and Southern Pho. I found that Pho even vary shop to shop in the same city.

Also, if you're a big crab / seafood fan, do some Ba/nh Canh Cua when you got time. To die for. So good. The closest thing I can describe Ba/nh Canh is Japanese Udon.

Thank you for visiting our country. But I want to say a few things that foreign friends still misunderstand about Vietnam. First, Vietnamese people are not like Chinese people. Because Vietnamese people have large, clear double eyelids since birth without the need for cosmetic surgery. While Chinese people do not have characteristic double eyelids. Therefore, I hope foreign friends do not misunderstand that Vietnamese people have eyes similar to East Asian people (Japanese, Korean, Chinese). We Vietnamese people are completely different from East Asians in terms of "eyes". You can come to Vietnam to verify what I say. You can go anywhere in Vietnam and meet many people with double eyelids. Second, Vietnam has a cold winter from October to March every year. That's all I wanted to say. Wishing you good health to explore other countries around the world
.Thank you. And I'm from Hanoi.
